text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on May 4 in history:
1471 - The Yorkists defeated the Lancastrians at the Battle of Tewkesbury in the Wars of the Roses.
1493 - Pope Alexander VI, a Spaniard, decreed that all new lands discovered west of the Azores were Spanish.
1654 - K'ang-hsi, fourth emperor of the Ch'ing dynasty, born.
1655 - Bartolommeo di Francesco Cristofori, Italian harpsichord, manufacturer, born. He was credited with designing the first pianoforte, which he called "the harpsichord that plays soft and loud".
1780 - The first Derby horse race was run at Epsom in England over a distance of one and a half miles.
1825 - Thomas Henry Huxley, British naturalist and humanist and originator of the word agnostic, was born.
1827 - John Hanning Speke, British explorer, born; he was the first European to see Lake Victoria, which he claimed was the source of the Nile.
1839 - The Cunard shipping line was founded by Samuel Cunard of Halifax, Nova Scotia.
1852 - The inspiration for Alice in Wonderland, Alice Liddell, was born the daughter of British scholar Henry Liddell.
1882 - Estelle Sylvia Pankhurst, British painter and suffragette, bore; she was the third member of her family to fight for votes for women.
1918 - Kakuei Tanaka, Japanese prime minister 1972-74, born. Disgraced later in the Lockheed bribery scandal, he was sentenced to four years in jail.
1925 - Luis Herrera Campins, Venezuelan president from 1978-84, born.
1926 - The first General Strike in British history began. It was called by the Trades Union Congress and troops were called in to man essential services.
1928 - Hosni Mubarak, President of Egypt since Anwar Sadat was assassinated in 1981, born.
1929 - Audrey Hepburn, British actress and Oscar winner for the "Roman Holiday", born. She was also noted for her roles in "Breakfast at Tiffany's" and "My Fair Lady".
1932 - Al Capone, U.S. "Public Enemy Number One", began his prison sentence for tax evasion after several appeals failed.
1938 - Dr Douglas Hyde became the first president of Ireland under its new constitution.
1942 - The battle of the Coral Sea started in World War Two, when naval and air battles began off the Solomon Islands.

1945 - Field Marshall Montgomery announced that all enemy forces in the Netherlands, North West Germany and Denmark had surrendered unconditionally; The U.S. 7th Army captured Hitler's country retreat of Berchtesgaden; Salzburg also captured by the Allies.
1955 - Georges Enescu, Romanian composer and violinist, died; among his pupils was Yehudi Menuhin.
1969 - Sir Francis Osbert Sacheverell Sitwell, author and member of famous British literary family, died.
1970 - National Guards shot four students dead and wounded 11 at Kent State University, after demonstrations against the Vietnam war.
1979 - Margaret Thatcher became Britain's first woman prime minister with a majority of 43 seats in the House of Commons.
1980 - Yugoslav wartime partisan leader Josip Broz Tito died aged 87. He became leader of the country in 1945 and president in 1953.
1982 - In the Falklands war, the British destroyer Sheffield was sunk by an Exocet missile killing 20.
1989 - Colonel Oliver North was found guilty in the investigations in the Iran-Contra affair.
1992 - About 70,000 Thais protested against the appointmentment of Suchinda Kraprayoon, an unelected general, as prime minister.
1993 - The U.S. handed over command of multinational forces in Somalia to the United Nations.

1994 - Israel and the PLO, overcoming a dramatic last-minute hitch, signed a historic agreement giving Palestinians in the occupied West Bank and Gaza Strip their first measure of freedom since the 1967 Middle East war.
1994 - The European Parliament overwhelmingly approved European Union plans to admit Austria, Finland, Norway and Sweden to the 12-nation bloc.
1996 - A 13-year era of Socialist rule ended in Spain when conservative leader Jose Maria Aznar was appointed prime minister.
